results.scenario: Admitted 3 nights for pneumonia; policy 2 years old.
results.rationale: Inpatient hospitalisation >24 hrs is covered; no waiting period issue at 2 years.
results.summary: The three‑night pneumonia hospitalisation is covered under the in‑patient hospitalisation clause, the initial waiting period is satisfied and no exclusion applies.
rejectionRisks: If the insured is 60 years or older, a 10 % co‑payment will be deducted (Section 4.2)
If pneumonia were deemed a pre‑existing disease (diagnosed within 48 months before policy start), the 36‑month pre‑existing disease waiting period would block payment (Section 3.3)
Room‑rent charges are subject to a cap of 1% of the Sum Insured per day (Section 4.1) which may reduce the payable amount

results.scenario: Hospitalised for dengue; policy started 15 days ago.
results.rationale: Any non-accident illness within the first 30 days is not payable.
results.summary: The claim is denied because the 30‑day initial waiting period for illnesses has not been met (policy is only 15 days old).
rejectionRisks: Initial waiting period not satisfied (policy age 15 days < 30 days required)

results.scenario: Broke a leg in a road accident; policy is 10 days old.
results.rationale: Initial 30-day waiting period does not apply to accidental hospitalisation.
results.summary: The broken leg from a road accident is covered because inpatient hospitalisation for injury is included and the initial waiting period does not apply to accidents.
rejectionRisks: Room‑rent charges exceeding the 1% of Sum Insured per day cap
Failure to provide accident proof (FIR/MLC) as required

results.scenario: Diabetic for 5 years; admitted for a diabetes complication; policy 12 months old.
results.rationale: Pre-existing disease covered only after 36 months of continuous cover.
results.summary: The diabetes complication hospitalisation is covered because it meets the in‑patient hospitalisation clause and all waiting periods and exclusions are satisfied.
rejectionRisks: If the insurer interprets diabetes as a pre‑existing disease despite the >48‑month gap, the 36‑month pre‑existing disease waiting period could block the claim.

results.scenario: Cataract surgery; policy 18 months old.
results.rationale: Cataract needs 24 months of continuous cover.
results.summary: Cataract surgery is excluded because the policy has a 24‑month specific‑illness waiting period and the policy is only 18 months old.
rejectionRisks: Specific‑illness waiting period not satisfied (policy age 18 months < 24‑month wait).

results.scenario: Cataract surgery; policy 3 years old.
results.rationale: Waiting period met, but cataract claims are capped at Rs 40,000 per eye.
results.summary: Cataract surgery is covered because the policy’s hospitalisation benefit applies and the 24‑month specific‑illness waiting period is satisfied, though the claim is subject to a Rs 40,000 per‑eye sub‑limit.
rejectionRisks: Cataract sub‑limit may reduce the payable amount to Rs 40,000 per eye

results.scenario: Father, 65, admitted for cardiac care; policy 4 years old.
results.rationale: Covered, but a 10% co-pay applies as insured is above 60.
results.summary: The cardiac hospitalisation is covered, but a 10% co‑payment and room‑rent caps will apply.
rejectionRisks: 10% co‑payment reduces the payable amount.
Room‑rent and ICU charges are capped at 1% and 2% of the Sum Insured per day respectively.

results.scenario: Chose a deluxe room costing above 1% of the sum insured.
results.rationale: Room rent capped at 1% of SI/day; higher category => proportionate payment.
results.summary: Deluxe room charges above the 1% daily cap are covered, but the insurer will pay only up to the capped amount proportionately.
rejectionRisks: Room‑rent cap limits payment to 1% of Sum Insured per day, so excess amount will not be reimbursed

results.scenario: Elective cosmetic nose reshaping.
results.rationale: Cosmetic/plastic surgery excluded unless due to accident, burn or cancer.
results.summary: Elective cosmetic nose reshaping is excluded under the policy’s cosmetic surgery exclusion.
rejectionRisks: Exclusion for cosmetic surgery (not accident/burn/cancer related).
Initial waiting period may not be satisfied if policy is less than 30 days old.

results.scenario: Reconstructive surgery after a burn injury.
results.rationale: Cosmetic exclusion has an explicit exception for burns.
results.summary: Reconstructive surgery after a burn is covered as an in‑patient hospitalisation expense, with the cosmetic‑surgery exclusion not applying because the surgery is necessitated by the burn.
rejectionRisks: If the burn is classified as an illness rather than an injury, the 30‑day initial waiting period could apply and reject the claim if policy age <30 days.
If the surgery is deemed purely cosmetic and not medically necessary for the burn, the exclusion in Section 5.2 would apply.
Room‑rent and ICU charges are subject to caps (1% and 2% of Sum Insured per day). Excess amounts will be reduced.
If the insured is over 60 years old, a 10% co‑payment will be deducted from the claim amount.

results.scenario: Root canal at the dentist; no accident involved.
results.rationale: Dental treatment excluded unless due to accident requiring hospitalisation.
results.summary: Root canal (dental) treatment is excluded because dental procedures are not covered unless caused by an accident and requiring hospitalisation.
rejectionRisks: Dental procedure excluded under policy exclusions

results.scenario: Jaw surgery with hospitalisation after a road accident.
results.rationale: Dental due to accident requiring hospitalisation is covered.
results.summary: Jaw surgery after a road accident is covered under the in‑patient hospitalisation benefit.

results.scenario: Admitted one day only for tests; no active treatment given.
results.rationale: Hospitalisation purely for diagnostics/observation is excluded.
results.summary: The admission was only for diagnostic tests with no active treatment, which is expressly excluded under the policy.
rejectionRisks: Exclusion for diagnostic-only hospitalisation without active treatment

results.scenario: Cataract done as a day-care procedure (<24 hrs); policy 3 years old.
results.rationale: Day-care covered and wait met, but the cataract sub-limit still applies.
results.summary: Cataract day‑care surgery is covered, the policy age exceeds the 24‑month specific‑illness waiting period, and no exclusion applies, though a Rs 40,000 per‑eye sub‑limit applies.
rejectionRisks: Cataract sub‑limit may reduce payable amount to Rs 40,000 per eye per policy year.

results.scenario: Normal delivery; policy 30 months old.
results.rationale: Maternity covered after 24 months; normal delivery limited to Rs 50,000.
results.summary: Normal delivery is covered after the 24‑month maternity waiting period, subject to the Rs 50,000 maternity limit.
rejectionRisks: Expense exceeds the Rs 50,000 normal‑delivery limit
Room‑rent or ICU charges exceed the caps set in Section 4.1

results.scenario: Delivery; policy 12 months old.
results.rationale: Maternity expenses need 24 months of continuous cover.
results.summary: Maternity expenses are not payable because the policy has only been in force for 12 months, which is less than the required 24‑month maternity waiting period.
rejectionRisks: Maternity waiting period not met (policy age 12 months < required 24 months)

results.scenario: Ambulance bill of Rs 3,500.
results.rationale: Road ambulance covered but capped at Rs 2,000 per hospitalisation.
results.summary: Ambulance charges are covered but only up to the Rs 2,000 sub‑limit, so the Rs 3,500 claim will be partially payable.
rejectionRisks: Amount exceeds the Rs 2,000 ambulance sub‑limit; excess Rs 1,500 may be denied.

results.scenario: Inpatient Ayurvedic treatment at a recognised hospital.
results.rationale: AYUSH in-patient treatment covered up to the sum insured.
results.summary: Ayurvedic inpatient treatment is covered, but the claim may be blocked by the 30‑day initial waiting period because the policy age is not provided.
rejectionRisks: Initial waiting period may not be satisfied (policy age < 30 days).

results.scenario: Rehab for alcohol dependence.
results.rationale: Treatment for alcoholism / substance abuse is excluded.
results.summary: Treatment for alcoholism is expressly excluded, so the rehab claim will not be payable.
rejectionRisks: Exclusion for alcoholism (Section 5.5) makes the claim non‑payable
Initial waiting period of 30 days may also apply if policy age is less than 30 days (Section 3.1)

results.scenario: Injury from a suicide attempt.
results.rationale: Self-inflicted injury / attempted suicide is excluded.
results.summary: The policy explicitly excludes expenses from self‑inflicted injury or suicide, so the claim is not payable.
rejectionRisks: Exclusion for self‑inflicted injury/suicide
Initial waiting period of 30 days may not be satisfied if policy age <30 days

results.scenario: Cost of new prescription glasses.
results.rationale: Spectacles, contact lenses and hearing aids are excluded.
results.summary: Prescription glasses are excluded under the policy’s exclusions.
rejectionRisks: Exclusion of spectacles expenses

results.scenario: Diagnostic tests 20 days before admission.
results.rationale: Pre-hospitalisation expenses covered up to 30 days before admission.
results.summary: Pre‑hospitalisation diagnostic tests 20 days before admission are covered, but it’s unclear whether the required initial waiting period has been satisfied because the policy age isn’t provided.
rejectionRisks: Initial waiting period may not be satisfied if policy is less than 30 days old

results.scenario: Medicines bought 75 days after discharge.
results.rationale: Post-hospitalisation covered only up to 60 days after discharge.
results.summary: Medicines purchased 75 days after discharge are outside the 60‑day post‑hospitalisation coverage window.
rejectionRisks: Expense incurred beyond the post‑hospitalisation 60‑day window
